items.title: 3.5 Real World Problems of Quadratic Equations and Inequalities

blocks.text: We shall now solve problems which, when expressed in symbols, lead to quadratic equations in one or two variables.
In order to solve such problems, we must:

items: Suppose the unknown quantities to be \(x\) or \(y\) etc.
Translate the problem into symbols and form the equations satisfying the given conditions.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
After these two steps of the book, finish every word problem with three more:
iii. Solve the equation (or inequality) by any method you know.
iv. Interpret: reject values that make no sense in the situation (a negative length, a fraction of a person) and attach units.
v. Check your answer against the words of the question, not only against the equation.
Useful translations: "is" \(\to\) \(=\); "greater than ... by 3" \(\to\) \(+3\); "at least" \(\to\) \(\ge\); "at most" \(\to\) \(\le\); area of a rectangle \(=\) length \(\times\) breadth.
The method of solving the problems will be illustrated through the following examples:

blocks.title: Example 9
blocks.problem: The length of a room is 3 metres greater than its breadth. If the area of the room is 180 square metres, find the length and the breadth of the room.
steps:
Given: length = breadth + 3 metres; area = 180 square metres.
To find: the length and the breadth of the room.
Method: let the breadth be \(x\); then the length is \(x + 3\). Area = length \(\times\) breadth gives a quadratic equation in \(x\). Solve it and keep only the value that makes sense for a length.

Step 1: Name the unknowns
Let the breadth of the room \(= x\) metres.
Then the length of the room \(= (x + 3)\) metres.
\[\text{Area} = x(x + 3)\ \text{m}^{2}\]
Why: the length is described in terms of the breadth, so one variable is enough (step i of the method).

Step 2: Form the equation
By the given condition:
\[x(x + 3) = 180 \quad \text{...(i)}\]
\[x^{2} + 3x - 180 = 0 \quad \text{...(ii)}\]
Why: this translates "the area is 180" into symbols (step ii). Expanding and moving 180 to the left gives the standard form.

Step 3: Factorise
We need two numbers whose product is \(-180\) and whose sum is \(3\): they are \(15\) and \(-12\).
\[x^{2} + 15x - 12x - 180 = 0\]
\[x(x + 15) - 12(x + 15) = 0\]
\[(x + 15)(x - 12) = 0\]
\[x = -15 \ \text{or}\ x = 12\]
Why: \(15 \times (-12) = -180\) and \(15 + (-12) = 3\), so splitting the middle term works.

Step 4: Reject the value that makes no sense
A breadth cannot be negative, so \(x = -15\) is not admissible. Hence \(x = 12\).
Why: the equation does not know it describes a room; we must apply the real-world meaning ourselves.

Step 5: Find the length
\[x + 3 = 12 + 3 = 15\]
Why: the length was defined as \(x + 3\).

Check:
Length \(-\) breadth \(= 15 - 12 = 3\) metres.
\[\text{Area} = 15 \times 12 = 180\ \text{m}^{2}\]
Both conditions of the question are satisfied.
blocks.answer: Breadth of the room = 12 metres and length of the room = 15 metres.

blocks.title: Example 10
blocks.problem: A company manufactures laptops and its weekly profit function (in thousands of dollars) is \(P(x) = -x^{2} + 2x + 3\), where \(x\) is the number of laptops produced (in hundreds). Find the range of production levels where the company makes at least \(\$4{,}000\) profit.
steps:
Given: \(P(x) = -x^{2} + 2x + 3\) (profit in thousands of dollars), \(x\) = laptops produced, in hundreds.
To find: the values of \(x\) for which the profit is at least \(\$4{,}000\).
Method: \(\$4{,}000\) is 4 thousand dollars, so "at least \(\$4{,}000\)" means \(P(x) \ge 4\). This is a quadratic inequality; simplify it and solve.

Step 1: Translate the condition
\[P(x) \ge 4\]
Why: \(P\) is measured in thousands of dollars, so \(\$4{,}000\) is the number 4; "at least" means "greater than or equal to".

Step 2: Substitute and bring everything to one side
\[-x^{2} + 2x + 3 \ge 4\]
\[-x^{2} + 2x + 3 - 4 \ge 0\]
\[-x^{2} + 2x - 1 \ge 0\]
Why: comparing with 0 makes the inequality easy to study.

Step 3: Multiply by \(-1\)
\[x^{2} - 2x + 1 \le 0\]
Why: multiplying an inequality by a negative number reverses its sign (\(\ge\) becomes \(\le\)). Now the \(x^{2}\) term is positive.

Step 4: Recognise a perfect square
\[(x - 1)^{2} \le 0\]
Why: \(x^{2} - 2x + 1 = x^{2} - 2(x)(1) + 1^{2} = (x - 1)^{2}\).

Step 5: Solve
The square of a real number is never negative: \((x - 1)^{2} \ge 0\) for every \(x\). So \((x - 1)^{2} \le 0\) holds only when
\[(x - 1)^{2} = 0 \Rightarrow x = 1\]
Why: a quantity that is both \(\ge 0\) and \(\le 0\) must be exactly 0.

Step 6: Interpret
\(x = 1\) means 1 hundred, i.e. 100 laptops. At this level the profit is exactly \(\$4{,}000\); at every other level it is less.
Why: the question is about laptops and dollars, so the answer must be given in those units.

Check:
\[P(1) = -1 + 2 + 3 = 4\]
\[P(0) = 3 < 4,\quad P(2) = 3 < 4\]
Completing the square: \(P(x) = 4 - (x - 1)^{2}\), so the largest possible profit is 4 (thousand dollars), reached only at \(x = 1\).
blocks.answer: The only production level is \(x = 1\), i.e. 100 laptops: the company makes exactly \(\$4{,}000\) profit there, and there is no production level where the profit is more than \(\$4{,}000\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Example 10 connects to 3.1.2: completing the square gives \(P(x) = -(x - 1)^{2} + 4\). The parabola opens downward with vertex \((1, 4)\), so 4 (thousand dollars) is the maximum profit. "At least the maximum" can only happen at the vertex itself, which is why the answer is a single production level and not an interval.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: In a word problem write a "Let ..." line for every unknown, state clearly why you reject a value ("breadth cannot be negative"), and give the final answer as a sentence with units. These lines carry marks.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
1. Let the unknown quantity be \(x\); express the other quantities in terms of \(x\).
2. Translate the conditions into an equation or inequality and bring it to standard form.
3. Solve, then keep only the values that make sense in the real situation.
4. "At least" means \(\ge\); multiplying an inequality by a negative number reverses it.
5. Answer in words with units and check against the question.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text:
1. Keeping a negative length or breadth as an answer.
2. Ignoring units: in Example 10, \(\$4{,}000\) is \(P = 4\) because \(P\) is in thousands, and \(x = 1\) means 100 laptops.
3. Forgetting to reverse the inequality sign when multiplying by \(-1\).
4. Stopping at \(x = 12\) without finding the length that the question also asks for.
